speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any rhythmic jerking movements of your limbs during these episodes of unresponsiveness?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Are these episodes triggered by flashing lights, reading, or specific situations, and do they occur more frequently when he is tired or stressed? Also, have you noticed any aura or specific sensory sensations before the staring begins?

REQUEST TEST: EEG (Electroencephalogram)
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electroencephalogram Findings: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side; MRI Brain Findings: No evidence of mass lesions, infarctions, or structural abnormalities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Temporal Lobe Epilepsy (specifically consistent with a focal seizure disorder, possibly including the olfactory/mucosal aura of "muddy taste").

The EEG confirms interictal epileptiform discharges in the right temporal lobe, which correlates perfectly with his semiological features of staring, automatisms (hand gestures), and a gustatory aura. Given the lack of structural abnormalities on the MRI, this is a primary electrical dysfunction of the right temporal lobe. We will proceed with anti-epileptic therapy and monitor for recurrence.
